reason: Moses is clearly portrayed as the established national leader of Israel in this passage. Multiple textual elements demonstrate this: (1) The entire congregation (כָּל־ עֲדַת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל) brings their collective grievances directly to him as the figure of authority; (2) God instructs Moses to 'go before the people' (עֲבֹר לִפְנֵי הָעָם) and to take the elders with him, establishing his hierarchical authority over the community leadership; (3) Moses functions as the mediator between God and the people, receiving divine commands and executing them; (4) He performs a divinely-mandated miraculous act before the elders to resolve a national crisis; (5) The people look to Moses specifically to solve their problems, indicating recognition of his leadership role. The text portrays him as an established national leader managing a crisis, not an aspiring leader.
